intro: Professionals and everyday users convert kilopascals (kPa) to bars (bar) when working across metric and metric standards in automotive tire inflation placards, hydraulic cylinder design, scuba diving tanks, and barometric weather tracking. One kilopascal equals 0.01 bars, while 1 bar equals 100 kilopascals. Whether you are verifying pressure specifications on imported equipment, cross-checking technical datasheets, or scaling practical measurements, this converter applies the exact NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 reference relationship with instant precision.

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: Gauge Pressure (psig) vs. Absolute Pressure (psia)
items: This converter scales pressure magnitude directly between kPa and bar. In automotive tires, HVAC, and compressed air systems, gauges display Gauge Pressure (referenced to ambient atmospheric pressure, ~14.696 psi or 101.325 kPa at sea level).
For thermodynamic gas laws (PV = nRT) or vacuum chamber calculations, convert gauge pressure to absolute pressure by adding local barometric pressure before scaling.

faqs.question: How many bars (bar) are in 1 kilopascal (kPa)?
faqs.answer: There are 0.01 bars (bar) in 1 kilopascal (kPa), which rounds to 0.01 bar for everyday calculations. Conversely, 1 bar equals 100 kilopascals.

faqs.question: How do I convert kilopascals to bars (kPa to bar)?
faqs.answer: To convert kilopascals to bars, use the formula: bar = kPa × 0.01. For example, converting 200 kPa gives 2 bar.

faqs.question: What is 200 kilopascals in bars?
faqs.answer: 200 kilopascals (kPa) equals exactly 2 bars (bar) using standard NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 conversion factors.
